messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: reseeding for NaN cases
parts:
Daniel and I just put in a patch that will try
random initialization up to 100 times if the random inits
do not lead to a finite log prob and to finite gradients for
all dimensions. (It's not checked in yet, but will be
in gm/command).

This approach will be repeatable under new seeds.

Does 100 seem like an OK number of attmepts? They're actually
not that expensive compared to sampling, so we could set it
higher. Or make it command-line configurable, I suppose.
(I want to resist adding new command-line options as much
as possible -- it makes it confusing to users -- maybe we
could tier them into basic and advanced if we need more.)

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] reseeding for NaN cases
parts:
Hah, teach me to not read all the emails :)  Ignore my previous email.

100 seems reasonable to me.  Really if even 2 don't work, it's probably a bug in model specification or in the range of the sampler relative to the parameters which goes back to my suggestion a while ago about being able to customize the initialization on a per model basis.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] reseeding for NaN cases
parts:
I've pushed the fix I mentioned yesterday, which should clear this
business up. (Good instincts, Marcus.)

I wonder if maybe it'd be useful to be able to specify an initial
value for epsilon on the command line without turning off step size
adaptation. Not a high priority, since the adaptation should be able
to cover a lot of ground in a small number of iterations, but might be
nice.

Matt
